summary.for_TEST_DESIGNER: Check especially: E2K-32 must assert the full CHROME_NOT_FOUND text on stderr (F1); a hang test for a handshake that never completes (F2); SMK-08 with two back-to-back loads (deviation 1) and a repeated series; E2K-17 with ok-ignore-term; E2K-13/14/15 via cdp.connect because launchBrowser rejects first; the slow START_EXITED path (~0.4 s) is inside the 5 s limit. findings.what: runAll prints an E2eError as `oneLine(error.message)`, so every multi-line message is cut to its first line. The design (4.1, 4.2, section 7 row 2, section 6 step 6: only the message of a NON-E2eError is cut to its first line) and tools/README.md ('a message that names SAI_CHROME and the places that were tried') say that when no Chrome is found the five numbered places are printed. Measured on a scratch copy (findChrome with PATH empty and exists false, run through runAll): stderr is `e2e: error=CHROME_NOT_FOUND: no Chrome or Chromium found. ... Places tried (5):` and the five lines are gone (findChrome itself builds them, checked). On the CI runner this is the log that branch B of criterion 10 and the owner read; criterion 2(d) is only met inside the function, not in what the user sees.
findings.fix: Print `error.message` in full for E2eError (keep oneLine only for the INTERNAL branch at line 345); the stack must still not be printed. The runner test E2K-32 should assert that a line `  5) chromium-browser (in PATH)` is on stderr.

findings.what: The WebSocket handshake to the browser has no time limit. Measured: a plain TCP server that accepts and never answers the upgrade leaves `connect()` pending for the whole 4 s of the probe (callTimeoutMs 500 is not used for opening). startTimeoutMs stops being counted at the port line (settle clears the timer), so a browser that prints the port line and then does not complete the upgrade hangs launchBrowser, and the preflight of runAll has no watchdog at all, until the 30-minute job limit. Q10: an external call has a timeout; design 4.5/4.6 promise 'no hang' for every browser fault.
findings.fix: Give connect a limit (use callTimeoutMs for the open, reject CALL_TIMEOUT or BROWSER_CLOSED and close the socket), or keep the start timer running until Browser.getVersion has answered. Add a stand-in mode that accepts TCP and never upgrades, and a test.

findings.what: `ERROR_CODES` and `usage()` are used by no file of the work (grep over tools/test/e2e and the stand-in); every USAGE error is built by `new E2eError("USAGE", ...)` by hand. Dead code unless TEST-DESIGNER uses ERROR_CODES to pin the table.
findings.fix: Delete `usage`; keep ERROR_CODES only if a test reads it, else delete it too.

findings.what: The same three helpers (is the group alive / signal the group / wait until it is gone) are written twice, with opposite polarity (`groupAlive` vs `groupGone`). One shared mechanism in two places is how AP-014 starts.
findings.fix: Move them to cleanup.js (it already owns the group registry) and import them in both.

findings.what: A PROTOCOL_ERROR of a poll is swallowed until the deadline and the WAIT_TIMEOUT message does not mention it; a persistent protocol error (a bad session) then reads as 'last value: undefined'. Behaviour not in the design (BACKEND-DEV note I4(f)).
findings.fix: Keep the last swallowed error and add its message to the WAIT_TIMEOUT text; record the rule in the design.

findings.what: On a start failure the code waits for stderr 'close' or 300 ms. Measured: START_EXITED always takes ~370-400 ms, i.e. the 300 ms timer always fires ('close' has already been emitted before the 'exit' listener is attached). Harmless (limit is 5 s) but the 'close' branch is dead in practice.
findings.fix: Check `child.stderr.destroyed` / `readableEnded` before waiting, or drop the 'close' listener and keep only the short timer.

findings.what: A failed screenshot write is reported with the code USAGE (a caller bug), which is the wrong code for an I/O failure; and `failure !== null && typeof failure === "object"` repeats the null check.
findings.fix: Use a code of the table that fits (or add one with a design note); drop the repeated condition.

findings.what: Deviation 1 is not in the design or in 0108 (see judgement). Needs a record so that the next reader does not remove it.
findings.fix: CODE-DESIGNER / ORCH: one sentence in design 4.8 (goto, reload) and a line in 0108 or the design change log; SMK-08 must run goto twice back to back.

deviation_judgements.deviation: (1) 100 ms wait after the load event in goto and reload
deviation_judgements.judgement: ACCEPTED, with Low F8. It is a real solution to a real Chrome race, not a hidden symptom: on a scratch copy with LOAD_SETTLE_MS=0, two back-to-back loads of the same page lost the favicon console line in 1 of 8 starts (the developer saw 3 of 3 under his conditions); with 100 ms 20 of 20 starts gave exactly one line. It costs 0.1 s per goto and is a time wait (no event exists for 'the favicon request was made'), which is the only weak point. It is not in the design and has no record: F8.

ACCEPTED. The design's E2K-17 uses hang-ignore-term, but that mode prints no port line, so no Browser exists to call close() on; the escalation SIGTERM -> SIGKILL of Browser.close can only be tested with a mode that starts and ignores SIGTERM. One line in the stand-in, section 5 allows added modes. Verified: ok-ignore-term close() finishes in ~0.7 s with the group gone. The design table row of E2K-17 should name the new mode (TEST-DESIGNER is told in summary).

deviation_judgements.deviation: (3) bad-json, error-object, no-answer make launchBrowser itself reject
deviation_judgements.judgement: ACCEPTED. It follows the design (4.6 step 5: Browser.getVersion is the first call), not a defect of the code. Measured with the stand-in: PROTOCOL_BAD_ANSWER / PROTOCOL_ERROR / CALL_TIMEOUT, each naming Browser.getVersion, group gone, folder gone, registry empty, next start works. Criterion 4(d) is met by the rejection of launchBrowser; E2K-13/14/15 should use cdp.connect directly for the 'pending calls' cases.
